scope: Named gooseberry cultivars for zone 6b: American (Ribes hirtellum-type), European (R. uva-crispa) and American × European hybrids, plus gooseberry × currant hybrids (jostaberry and similar). Plain currants and unnamed species plants are left out. NJ allows gooseberries into Hunterdon County; only a few Sussex, Passaic and Morris County townships are closed to them.

varieties.name: Hinnonmaki Red
varieties.summary: Finnish red gooseberry; sweet-tart, mildew resistant, the most widely sold.
varieties.description: A Finnish cultivar (Lepaan Punainen) of European × American parentage. Medium-large dark red berries, sweet flesh under a tart skin, good fresh; a thorny, mid-size bush resistant to powdery mildew, ripening early to mid-season.

varieties.name: Hinnonmaki Yellow
varieties.summary: Finnish yellow-green gooseberry with an aromatic, apricot-like flavor.
varieties.description: A Finnish cultivar whose green berries turn yellow in sun, prized for aromatic flavor. Compact, thorny bush with some resistance to mildew and leaf spot; mid-season.

varieties.name: Invicta
varieties.summary: English green gooseberry; heavy crops, mildew resistant, RHS AGM.
varieties.description: Bred at East Malling Research Station, England, from Resistenta × Whinham's Industry. Large green berries for cooking or fresh eating, very heavy crops; vigorous, spreading and very thorny, with resistance to American gooseberry mildew; early to mid-season.

varieties.name: Pixwell
varieties.summary: North Dakota classic; pink-purple pie berry, few thorns, very hardy.
varieties.description: Released in 1932 by the North Dakota Agricultural Experiment Station from Oregon Champion × Ribes missouriense. Medium berries ripen green to pink and purple-red, tart and good for pies; nearly thornless, very hardy and mildew resistant; mid to late season.

varieties.name: Poorman
varieties.summary: Utah heirloom (c. 1890); sweet red berries good fresh.
varieties.description: An American gooseberry from Brigham City, Utah (about 1890), from Houghton × Downing. Medium-large red berries sweet enough to eat fresh; vigorous, productive, thorny bush with good mildew resistance; mid-season.

varieties.name: Captivator
varieties.summary: Canadian nearly thornless gooseberry; pink-red teardrop berries.
varieties.description: Bred in Ottawa, Canada (released 1950s) from American × European parents. Teardrop berries ripen from pale green to burgundy-red, mildly sweet; nearly thornless with good mildew resistance; early to mid-season.

varieties.name: Tixia
varieties.summary: Swiss nearly thornless red; upright bush that's easy to pick.
varieties.description: A Swiss gooseberry (about 1990) from Invicta × a mildew-resistant selection. Large red berries on semi-thornless, upright shoots that make picking easy; mildew resistant.

varieties.name: Black Velvet
varieties.summary: Late, dark purple berries with a grape-like flavor.
varieties.description: A dark purple to near-black hybrid derived in part from the coastal black gooseberry (Ribes divaricatum). Small to medium berries with a sweet, grape- or blueberry-like flavor; upright, thorny, hardy bush; late-ripening.

varieties.name: Jeanne
varieties.summary: USDA release (2006); sweet late red, resists mildew and rust.
varieties.description: Introduced in 2006 by the USDA-ARS National Clonal Germplasm Repository in Corvallis, Oregon. Large, thin-skinned dark red dessert berries on a compact bush that blooms and ripens late; reported resistant to powdery mildew, white pine blister rust and leaf spot.

varieties.name: Jahn's Prairie
varieties.summary: Alberta prairie selection; very hardy, few thorns, shade tolerant.
varieties.description: A selection of the Canadian gooseberry (Ribes oxyacanthoides) found in Alberta around 1984. Pinkish-red berries on a compact bush with few thorns, hardy to about −40°F and able to fruit in part shade; mid-season, disease resistant.

varieties.name: Amish Red
varieties.summary: American heirloom; productive, mildew-free red berries.
varieties.description: An American heirloom of unrecorded origin, associated with Amish growers. Medium red berries on a large, productive bush that resists mildew; mid-season.

varieties.name: Glenndale
varieties.summary: USDA 1932 release for hot summers; small dark purple berries.
varieties.description: Bred by the USDA at Glenn Dale, Maryland and released in 1932 from Ribes missouriense × European gooseberry, aimed at hot southern summers. Small dark red-purple berries on a tall, fountain-shaped, vigorous bush.

varieties.name: Welcome
varieties.summary: Minnesota 1957 release; few thorns, resists mildew and rust.
varieties.description: An American gooseberry released in Minnesota in 1957. Medium pink-red, tart berries on a bush with few thorns and resistance to mildew and white pine blister rust; early to mid-season.

varieties.name: Sabine
varieties.summary: Ottawa-bred, few thorns; pinkish berries.
varieties.description: A gooseberry from the Ottawa, Canada program (Spinefree × Clark). Pinkish to burgundy berries on a hardy bush with few thorns, resistant to mildew and white pine blister rust.

varieties.name: Whitesmith
varieties.summary: English heirloom (c. 1824); pale green-white dessert berry.
varieties.description: An English dessert gooseberry introduced about 1824. Medium, oval, pale green to whitish berries with good flavor on a dense upright bush; resists white pine blister rust but is prone to mildew.

varieties.name: Leepared
varieties.summary: Heavy-bearing Finnish red gooseberry.
varieties.description: A heavy-bearing Finnish red gooseberry sold by Raintree. The name may be a variant spelling of Lepaa Red (Hinnonmaki Red); tracked separately because Raintree sells both.

varieties.name: Little Ben
varieties.summary: Compact, very productive red gooseberry.
varieties.description: A compact gooseberry sold for its heavy crops and ornamental habit. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Selby
varieties.summary: Named gooseberry sold by One Green World.
varieties.description: A named gooseberry sold by One Green World. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Friend
varieties.summary: Ukrainian burgundy gooseberry sold as nearly thornless.
varieties.description: A Ukrainian hybrid with burgundy berries, sold as Friend Red™ Thornless. Nearly spineless canes; can be prone to leaf spot.

varieties.name: Jewel
varieties.summary: Polish dwarf gooseberry with burgundy fruit.
varieties.description: A dwarf gooseberry of Polish origin with burgundy berries. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Oregon Champion
varieties.summary: Oregon 1876 heirloom; green-yellow berries.
varieties.description: Raised by O. Dickinson in Salem, Oregon in 1876 from Crown Bob × Houghton. Medium green berries that turn sweeter and yellow-green when fully ripe; thorny, about 5 ft, somewhat mildew prone.

varieties.name: Red Jacket
varieties.summary: Late green berries with a red blush; vigorous bush.
varieties.description: An older gooseberry also sold as ‘Comanche’. Green berries blushed red, ripening late on a vigorous, upright bush with some disease resistance.

varieties.name: Whinham's Industry
varieties.summary: English heirloom dark red dessert berry; RHS AGM.
varieties.description: A British heirloom with large, sweet, dark red berries for dessert or cooking. Vigorous and upright, tolerant of part shade and clay, but susceptible to American gooseberry mildew; late season.

varieties.name: Leveller
varieties.summary: Classic English yellow dessert berry (c. 1851); RHS AGM.
varieties.description: An English dessert gooseberry dating to about 1851. Very large golden-green berries with excellent flavor, mid-season; needs fertile soil and is hard to grow well in hot, humid summers.

varieties.name: Orus 8
varieties.summary: Gooseberry × black currant hybrid; near-black berries, rust resistant.
varieties.description: A gooseberry × black currant hybrid. Very vigorous, healthy bush with heavy crops of medium, almost black berries; rust resistant.

varieties.name: Jostaberry (Josta)
varieties.summary: German black currant × gooseberry hybrid; thornless, vigorous.
varieties.description: A black currant × gooseberry hybrid developed in Germany, completed by Rudolf Bauer at the Erwin Baur Institute. Near-black berries between a gooseberry and a currant in size, tasting of both; large, thornless, mildew- and rust-resistant bush.

varieties.name: Red Josta
varieties.summary: Red-fruited jostaberry.
varieties.description: A red-fruited jostaberry-type hybrid. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Jostine
varieties.summary: Thornless jostaberry selection.
varieties.description: A thornless jostaberry-type black currant × gooseberry selection. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Giant Jostaberry
varieties.summary: Large-fruited, rust-resistant jostaberry.
varieties.description: A large-fruited black currant × gooseberry hybrid sold by Raintree as rust resistant. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Shefford
varieties.summary: Thornless European x American cross; large golden-yellow, sweet berries.
varieties.description: A gooseberry of Canadian origin held at the USDA National Clonal Germplasm Repository in Corvallis, Oregon, from a European x North American cross. Large golden-yellow berries, sweet and crisp; thornless, disease-resistant bush reaching 3-5 ft; ripens June-July.

varieties.name: Red George
varieties.summary: Ukrainian gooseberry with very dark red, sweet fruit on a compact bush.
varieties.description: A Ukrainian gooseberry sold by One Green World. Very dark red, sweet berries, roughly 4-5 lbs per plant annually, ripening in July; compact bush reaching 2-3 ft.

varieties.name: Siewka K1
varieties.summary: Polish gooseberry; purplish-red, sweet berries on a compact, disease-resistant bush.
varieties.description: A Polish gooseberry cultivar sold by One Green World, among its European x American (R. uva-crispa x R. hirtellum) hybrid offerings. Purplish-red, sweet berries on a compact 2-3 ft bush; disease resistant, bearing within 1-2 years, ripening June-July.
